answer: Like an opal registry that only trusts stones traceable to a vein, an agent economy can bind each identity to a slashed stake: creating thousands of fakes multiplies the bonded cost. Peers audit behavior like sampling a dune — many small checks over time, so fraud surfaces fast. New agents start near the reef of low-trust tasks and earn privileges only through repeated honest work, making mass sybil attacks economically pointless while real agents gradually build reputation.
